bridge.yt_desc:
London opened a brand-new footbridge, 90,000 people walked across it, and two days later it was closed. Nothing was broken: the crowd itself was making it sway.

Would you have crossed on day one? A or B 👇

Sources:
• Wikipedia, Millennium Bridge, London (opening, closure, synchronous lateral excitation, dampers, reopening): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Bridge,_London
• AISC Modern Steel Construction, "Dynamic results" (2002): https://www.aisc.org/globalassets/modern-steel/archives/2002/08/2002v08_dynamic_results.pdf
• Londonist, 11 interesting facts about the Millennium Bridge: https://londonist.com/london/features/millennium-bridge-trivia

hans.yt_desc:
A horse in Berlin seemed to do arithmetic by tapping his hoof, and a panel of 13 experts found no trick. Then one young scientist asked a question he didn't know the answer to.

Could Hans read you? A or B 👇

Sources:
• Wikipedia, Clever Hans (the 1904 commission, Oskar Pfungst's tests: 89% correct when Hans could see the questioner, 6% when he couldn't): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clever_Hans
• Samhita & Gross, "The Clever Hans Phenomenon revisited", Communicative & Integrative Biology (2013): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3921203

The skeptic's lines are a dramatized retelling; the facts are from the sources above.

raft.yt_desc:
A ship's steward survived 133 days alone on a small wooden raft in the Atlantic: a nail became a fishing hook, his life jacket caught rain, and a shark became something to drink.

Day one on that raft: what do you save first? A or B 👇

Sources:
